Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 10, verse 2:

Ibn ʿAbbas said, in the narration of al-Walibi from him, regarding His words: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure standing (qadama sidq) with their Lord﴾

He said: "Happiness was decreed for them in the first remembrance (al-dhikr al-awwal)."

This does not contradict the view of those who said it refers to the good deeds they sent forward, nor the view of those who said it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). For happiness was decreed for them by God in the first remembrance, through their deeds at the hands of Muhammad (ﷺ). So it is a good that God caused to precede them, then He sent it forward for them at the hands of His Messenger, and then He will bring them forward to Him on the day of their meeting with Him.

(A benefit)

Consider the words of the Exalted: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind that We have revealed to a man from among them: "Warn mankind, and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure standing with their Lord"? The disbelievers said: "Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer."﴾

Why was the verb of saying not joined by a conjunction? Because it serves as an explanation of their astonishment and as an apposition (badal) to His words: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind﴾. It therefore follows the pattern of His words: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty (athaman). The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation (muhanan)﴾. Since the doubling of punishment is an apposition and explanation of "athaman," it is not good to join it to that by a conjunction.

(Section)

As for qadam al-sidq (a sure standing): it has been explained as Paradise, as Muhammad (ﷺ), and as the good deeds.

The reality of "qadam" is what they sent forward, and what they will come upon on the Day of Resurrection. They sent forward the deeds and the faith in Muhammad (ﷺ), and they will come upon Paradise, which is the recompense for that.

Whoever explained it as Paradise meant: what they will come upon. Whoever explained it as the deeds and the Prophet (ﷺ) meant: because they sent them forward, and they sent forward faith in him before them. So all three are a sure standing.

(Section)

Consider the states of this sun in its descent and ascent, establishing these times and seasons, and the benefits and wisdoms within them. For if the whole of time were a single season, the benefits of the remaining seasons would be lost.

If it were all summer, the benefits of winter would be lost; and if it were all winter, the benefits of summer would be lost. Likewise, if it were all spring or all autumn: in winter, heat recedes into the interiors of bodies, the depths of the earth and the mountains, so that the materials of fruits and other things are generated; the surfaces grow cold, and the air condenses within it, so that clouds, rain, snow and hail arise, by which the earth and its inhabitants live; and by it the bodies of animals grow strong and their powers increase, and the natural faculties multiply, and what the heat of summer dissolved in bodies is replaced.

In spring the natures are stirred, and the materials generated in winter appear, so plants emerge, trees blossom with flowers, and animals are moved to reproduction.

In summer the air becomes intensely hot and very warm, so fruits ripen; the bodily wastes and humours that had been bound together in winter are dissolved, and the cold recedes and flees into the interiors.

For this reason springs and wells become cold, and the stomach does not digest the heavy foods that it used to digest in winter, because it used to digest them with the heat that had settled in the bellies. When summer came, the heat moved out to the surface of the body, and the cold withdrew from it. When autumn comes, the time becomes moderate, the air clears and cools, and that scorching wind is broken; God, in His wisdom, made it a barrier between the scorching of summer and the cold of winter, lest the animal pass in one instant from intense heat to intense cold, and so feel its harm and suffer greatly from it. When it moves to it gradually and in order, it is not hard for it, for at every stage it prepares to receive what is more intense than it, until the sharpness of cold arrives after preparation and acceptance: a wisdom far-reaching and a sign striking. Likewise, spring is a barrier between winter and summer, in which animals move from the cold of this to the heat of that, gradually and in order. So blessed is God, Lord of the worlds, and the best of creators.

(Section)

Then consider the state of the sun and the moon and the light and illumination they have deposited, and how God made for them mansions and stations, which they traverse stage after stage, to establish the state of the year and to complete the benefits of reckoning for the world, of which people have no independence from their interests. Through this one knows the reckoning of lifespans and the appointed terms of debts, leases, transactions, counting, and other things.

Were it not for the sun and moon's passing through those mansions and their movement through them, station after station, nothing of that would be known.

Exalted is He, has alerted to this in more than one place in His Book, as in His saying: ﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it stations, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. God did not create that except in truth; He explains the signs for a people who know﴾ (5).

And the Exalted said: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day to see, that you might seek bounty from your Lord, and that you might know the number of years and the reckoning﴾.

Then consider the wisdom in the sun's rising over the world, how the Mighty, the All-Knowing, glorified is He, determined it. For if it rose at one point in the sky and stood there without passing beyond it, its rays would not reach many regions, because the shadow of one side of the sphere of the earth would screen it from the other side; night would be perpetual for those over whom it did not rise, and day perpetual for those over whom it was rising, and both would be corrupted.

So divine wisdom and lordly care required that it rise at the beginning of the day from the east, shining upon what faces it on the western horizon; then it never ceases to revolve, covering one region after another until it reaches the west, shining upon what had been hidden from it at the beginning of the day. Thus night and day alternate for them, and their interests are ordered.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 10, verse 11:

The early scholars (al-Salaf) said: It is a person's supplication against himself, his children, and his family in a state of anger. If God, exalted is He, were to answer it, He would destroy him and destroy those against whom he prays. But He does not answer it, because He knows that the one supplicating did not truly intend it.

Consider these two decisive proofs contained within this concise expression. The first: this (revelation) is from God, not from me; it is not within my power, nor of the kind of thing humans are capable of. And if God, glory be to Him, had willed, He would have withheld from it my heart, my tongue, your hearing and your understanding, so that I would not have been able to recite it to you, nor would you have been able to comprehend and understand it.

The second proof: I have remained among you for a lifetime until the time I brought it to you, while you have witnessed me, known my circumstances, accompanied me at home and on journeys, known my affairs both minor and major, and verified my conduct. Was it the conduct of one who is among the most lying, most wicked, and most unjust of creatures? For there is no one more lying, more unjust, or of more vile conduct than one who openly defies his Lord, opposes Him with falsehood and fabrication against Him, seeks to corrupt the world, oppresses souls, and transgresses in the earth without right.

Moreover, you know that I did not read any book, nor did I write one with my right hand, nor did I keep company with anyone from whom I learned. Rather, I accompanied you on your journeys, to those from whom you learn and whom you ask about the reports of nations, kings, and other things, and in no way did I take part with you in them. Then I brought you this momentous news, which contains the knowledge of the first and the last, and the knowledge of what has been and what will be, in detail.

So what proof is clearer than this, and what expression is more eloquent and concise than this expression that encompasses it?

Then I brought you this momentous news, which contains the knowledge of the first and the last, and the knowledge of what has been and what will be, in detail.

So what proof is clearer than this, and what expression is more eloquent and concise than this expression that encompasses it?

(Benefit)

As for the contradiction between the all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, and having a son, it requires a specific understanding. Its formulation is that it is said: If He had a son, He would know him, for He is All-Knowing of everything. And Allah, exalted is He, does not know of any son for Himself. So it is impossible that He should have a son whom He does not know. This is an argument from the negation of His knowledge of a thing to the negation of that thing itself, for if it existed He would know it; since He does not know it, it does not exist. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which can neither harm them nor benefit them﴾ [Qur'an 10:18], the verse.

This is a negation of what they claimed concerning intercessors, by negating the Lord's knowledge of them, which entails the negation of the known. The enemies of Allah cannot be obstinate and say that Allah knows that such things exist, because He, exalted is He, knows only the existence of what He has brought into being and its reality, and He knows that He will bring into being what He wills to create. So He knows Himself and His attributes, and He knows His creatures which have entered existence and ceased, those which have entered existence and remained, and those which have not yet come into being. As for something else that is neither created by Him nor subject to His lordship, the Lord, exalted is He, does not know it, because it is impossible in itself. Thus He knows it as impossible, not as an actual existent, for if He knew it as an actual existent, knowing it would be the same as ignorance, and that is among the greatest impossibilities.

These are the proofs of the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, against the falsehoods attributed to Him by His enemies and by those who fabricate against Him. So weigh them against the lengthy and broad arguments of the theologians, which are like the *ḍarī'* (a thorny plant) that neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. When you weigh the two, the superiority becomes evident to you, if you are perceptive; and whoever is blind in this life will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in the way. So praise be to Allah, who has made His believing servants independent, through His Book, of the proofs He has deposited in it, and through its clarification, of the boastful talk of the theologians and the babbling of the bewildered. The blessing of Allah upon a servant whom He has made independent, through understanding His Book, from need of anything else is indeed great. ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them? Indeed in this is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe﴾ [Qur'an 29:51].

(Diversity and Plurality of the Winds)

Among this category is the mention of the winds in the Qur'an, both in the plural and in the singular. Wherever they occur in the context of mercy, they come in the plural; and wherever they occur in the context of punishment, they come in the singular. The secret of this is that the winds of mercy differ in their attributes, their directions, and their benefits. When one of them stirs, He creates for it what opposes it, something that breaks its force and blunts its sharpness, so that from the two of them there arises a gentle wind that benefits animals and plants. Thus every wind of mercy has opposite it something that balances it and turns back its force. Therefore, in the context of mercy, they are called "winds" (riyāḥ, plural). As for punishment, it comes from one direction and in one stream; nothing stands against it, and nothing else opposes it, until it reaches where it was commanded to go. It is not turned back, and its sharpness is not broken. So it carries out what it was commanded and strikes what it was sent to. For this reason, He, glorified is He, described the wind He sent upon 'Ad as barren, saying: ﴿We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, which is the one that does not fertilize and has no good in it, and which renders barren whatever it passes over. Then consider how this pattern holds consistently, except in His saying in Surat Yunus: ﴿He is the One who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, there comes upon them a violent wind﴾.

So He mentioned the wind of good mercy in the singular, because the completeness of mercy there is achieved only through the unity of the wind, not through its diversity. For a ship does not move except by one wind, coming from one direction. When winds differ upon ships and collide and oppose one another, that is the cause of destruction. What is sought there is one wind, not multiple winds. He emphasized this meaning by describing it as good, to dispel the assumption that it might be a stormy wind; rather, it is one in which one rejoices because of its goodness. So let the discerning person take in with his insight these blossoming, wondrous gardens that make hearts dance with joy, and be nourished by them instead of food and drink. Praise be to God, the Opener, the All-Knowing. Such a section must be held fast to with the molars, and the fingers should be folded over it, for it will lead you to the secrets of wonders you gather from the words of God. And God is the Granter of success to what is right.

(Section)

He, glorified is He, speaks of the winds of mercy in the plural form because of the difference in their benefits and what arises from them. One wind stirs the clouds, one fertilizes them, one carries them upon its backs, and one nourishes plants. Since the winds differ in their directions and natures, He made for every wind an opposing wind that breaks its force and sharpness, while its gentleness and mercy remain. So the winds of mercy are multiple. As for the wind of punishment, it is a single wind sent from one direction to destroy what it is sent to destroy. No other wind stands against it to oppose it and break its force or repel its sharpness; rather, it is like a great army that nothing can withstand, destroying everything it comes upon. Consider the wisdom, majesty, and eloquence of the Qur'an: how this pattern holds on land. As for the sea, the wind of mercy there came in the singular, as in His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿He is the One who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, there comes upon them a violent wind, and the waves come upon them from every place﴾.

Indeed, ships only move by a single wind coming from one direction. When winds differ upon ships and oppose one another, their movement is not completed. So the purpose of them at sea is the opposite of their purpose on land, since at sea the purpose is that the wind be one, good, and not opposed by anything. Thus it is mentioned in the singular here and in the plural on land. Then, He, glorified is He, gave this subtle creation, which is moved by the weakest of creatures and which tears through them, such force, strength, and might that it disturbs solid, strong, resistant bodies, drives them from their places, breaks them into pieces, and carries them upon its back. Consider it, with its subtlety and lightness: if it enters a waterskin, for example, and fills it, then a heavy body such as a man or other is placed upon it and presses down to submerge it in water, it cannot. And if one places heavy solid iron on the surface of water, it sinks into it. This subtle thing refused to be overcome by the water, while the strong and mighty did not refuse it. By this wisdom, God, glorified is He, keeps ships afloat on the surface of water despite their weight and the weight of what they carry. Likewise, every hollow body in which air is contained does not sink, because air refuses to be submerged in water, so the loaded, laden ship clings to it.

Consider how this great heavy body sought refuge in this subtle, light thing and clung to it until it was safe from drowning. This is like one who falls into a well and grasps the hem of a strong, mighty man who holds back from falling into the well, and so he is saved by clinging to him. Glory be to Him who suspended this great, heavy vessel by this subtle air, without any visible tie or knot.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 10, verse 24:

God, glorified is He, likens the life of this world to the situation in which it adorns itself before the eye of the beholder, so that it delights him with its finery and pleases him, and he inclines toward it and loves it, deceived by it. Then, when he thinks that he owns it and is able to control it, it is suddenly taken from him at the moment when he needs it most, and he is cut off from it. He likened it to land on which rain falls, so that it sprouts, its plants flourish, and its appearance pleases the beholder, who is deceived by it and thinks that he is able to control it and owns it. Then the command of God comes, and a blight suddenly strikes its plants, so that it becomes as though it had never been before. His hopes are disappointed, and his hands are left empty of it. Thus is the condition of this world and of the one who trusts in it, the same. This is among the most eloquent of comparisons and analogies.

(Faidah)

What is intended here is that the order (of the verse) is the order of detail following generalities. It is a logical (ʿilmī) order, not an external (khārijī) one, for the mind first perceives a thing in summary and then seeks its detail afterward. In external reality, however, it occurs only in detail. So reflect on this point, which has been hidden from many people, to the extent that they thought the order in the verse is like the order of reporting, as if to say: "We informed you of this before that."

(Fasl)

Some of them divided the Sufis (al-Sufiyyah) into four categories: the People of the Precedences (aṣḥāb al-sawābiq), the People of the Outcomes (aṣḥāb al-ʿawāqib), the People of the Moment (aṣḥāb al-waqt), and the People of Truth (aṣḥāb al-ḥaqq). He said:

As for the People of the Precedences, their hearts are always fixed upon what was preordained for them by God, knowing that the eternal judgment does not change through the acquisition of the servant.

They say: "Whomever the precedences have distanced, the means will not bring near." So their thought on this is constant. Yet, along with this, they strive in carrying out the commands, avoiding the prohibitions, and drawing near to God through various kinds of acts of devotion, without relying on them or paying them any heed. One of them says:

"How can I please You, unless You grant me success?
Far, far away! Success does not come from me."

"If there is no precedence for me in what is decreed,
then the deeds I have done will not benefit me."

As for the People of the Outcomes, they reflect on how their affair will end, for affairs are judged by their final stages, deeds by their conclusions, and the outcome is hidden, as it has been said:

"Let not the clarity of the times deceive you,
for beneath it lie hidden calamities."

How many a spring has had its trees bloom, its flowers open, and its fruits become beautiful, only for a heavenly disaster to strike it shortly afterward, so that it became as God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and become beautified, and its people think they have power over it﴾ [Yunus: 24], up to His saying ﴿they reflect﴾ [Yunus: 24].

"How many an aspirant has been thrown by the steed of his resolve,
so that he fell prostrate on his hands and his face."

It was said to one of them, when a behavior contrary to what was known of him was observed: "What has befallen you?" He said: "A veil has descended," and he recited:

"You had a good opinion of the days when they were good,
and did not fear the evil that fate might bring.
The nights made peace with you, so you were deceived by them,
yet at the clarity of the nights, turbidity arises."

The wonder is not at the one who perished, asking how he perished. Rather, the wonder is at the one who was saved, asking how he was saved.

"You marvel at my sickness,
but my health is the wonder."

Those who turn back on their heels are many times more numerous than those who have braved the steep path (al-ʿaqabah):

"Take one from a thousand,
and cast aside all the rest after him."

As for the People of the Moment, they have not occupied themselves with precedences or outcomes, but with observing the moment and what its judgments require of them. They said: "The knower is the son of his moment; he has no past and no future."

One of them saw Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) in a dream, and said to him: "Advise me." He said to him: "Be the son of your moment."

As for the People of Truth, they are with the Lord of the moment and of time, its owner and its manager. They are absorbed in witnessing Him rather than in contemplating the moments, and they have no leisure to observe any moment or time. As it has been said:

"I do not know whether my night has grown long or not;
how can one know this who is preoccupied with it?"

"If I had leisure to dwell on the length of my night,
and to watch the stars, I would be idle."

"Indeed, for lovers, the brevity of the night,
and its length, both are occupation enough through love."

Al-Junayd said: "I entered upon al-Sarī one day, and I said to him: 'How have you risen this morning?' He began to recite:

'I have neither relief in the day nor in the night,
so I do not care whether the night has been long or short.'"

Then he said: "With your Lord there is neither night nor day."

He is alluding to the fact that he is not longing for the times, but is with the One who ordained the night and the day.

(Fasl)

As for (ḥattā) ["until"], it is established to indicate that what follows it is the limit (ghāyah) of what precedes it. The limit of anything is its boundary, and for this reason its letters resemble the word for boundary (ḥadd): it is a ḥāʾ before two tāʾs, just as ḥadd comes before two dāls. The dāl is like the tāʾ in place of articulation and in quality, except in voicing. So because it is voiced, the ḥāʾ is more fitting to be a noun (ism) for its strength, and the tāʾ, because it is unvoiced, is more fitting to be a letter (ḥarf) for its weakness. And since ḥattā indicates a limit, they put it in the genitive, just as they put in the genitive with (ilā) ["to"], which also indicates a limit. The difference between them is that ḥattā is the limit of what precedes it and is part of it, whereas what follows ilā is not part of what precedes it, but the end of what precedes the particle is reached at it. For this reason, ilā differs from it in most of its rulings, and ilā is not a coordinating particle (ʿāṭifah), because what follows it is disconnected from what precedes it, unlike ḥattā. For this reason ḥattā entered among the coordinating particles (ḥurūf al-ʿaṭf). It is not permissible for it to enter upon a genitive pronoun, since it is a particle that governs in the genitive; you do not say qāma al-qawmu ḥattāka ["the people stood, until you"], just as you do not say qāmū wa-k. And since what follows it is the limit of what precedes it, it is not permissible in coordination to say qāma Zaydun ḥattā ʿAmrun ["Zayd stood, until ʿAmr"], nor akaltu khubzan ḥattā tamran ["I ate bread, until dates"], because the second is neither a limit of the first nor a time-frame for it.

(Tanbīh)

What is meant by the fact that ḥattā indicates the endpoint, and that what follows it is a time-frame (ẓarf), is not that what follows it must come later in the action than what precedes it. When you say māta al-nāsu ḥattā al-anbiyāʾu ["the people died, even the prophets"], and qadima al-ḥujjājū ḥattā al-mushāt ["the pilgrims arrived, even those on foot"], it does not necessarily follow that the death of the prophets came after the people's death, or that the arrival of those on foot came after the pilgrims' arrival. For this reason some people have said: "ḥattā is like the wāw (and), differing from it only in two respects. The first is that the coordinated term must be of the same category as the term coordinated with it, so you cannot say qadima al-nāsu ḥattā al-khayl ["the people arrived, even the horses"], unlike with wāw. The second is that it differs from it by being stronger, weaker, greater, or lesser."

As for whether it conveys the notion of limit and boundary, it does not. What led them to this view is the two examples mentioned above, but he missed knowing the meaning of what follows it being a limit and a time-frame. Know, therefore, that what is meant is that it is a limit within the thing coordinated with, not within the action itself, for it must differ from it in intensity, weakness, scarcity, or abundance. When you understand this, the prophets are the limit of "the people" in nobility and virtue, and those on foot are the limit of "the pilgrims" in weakness and incapacity. When you say akaltu al-samakata ḥattā raʾsahā ["I ate the fish, even its head"], the head is the limit of the fish's consumption, but it is not meant that the head was the end of your eating; rather, it is permissible for your eating of the head to have come first. This is something that many grammarians overlooked and did not point out.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 10, verse 25–26:

Since the world is exposed to these calamities, while Paradise is free from them, He said: ﴿And Allah calls to the abode of peace﴾.

Here He named it "the abode of peace" because of its safety from these calamities mentioned in the world. He made the call to it general, and He specified guidance for whomever He wills. That is His justice, and this is His grace.

(Benefit)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah calls to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾. He made His call general, encompassing clarification and indication, and He specified His guidance as success (tawfiq) and inspiration (ilham).

(Section)

There has been disagreement about naming Paradise "the abode of peace" (dar al-salam). It has been said: "al-Salam" is Allah, and Paradise is His abode.

It has been said: "al-Salam" is safety (al-salamah), and Paradise is the abode of safety from every calamity, defect and deficiency.

It has been said: it was named "the abode of peace" because their greeting therein is "peace" (salam). These meanings are not mutually contradictory.

(Subtle point)

Regarding the attribution of Paradise to "peace," there are three opinions:

The first: it is an attribution to its Owner, al-Salam, glory be to Him.

The second: it is an attribution to the greeting of its people, for their greeting therein is "peace."

The third: it is an attribution to the meaning of peace, i.e., the abode of peace from every calamity, deficiency and evil. The three are interrelated, although the third is the most apparent. For if the attribution were to its Owner, it would have been attributed to a name of His other than "peace," and it would be said "the abode of the Merciful," or "the abode of Allah," or "the abode of the King," and similar.

Moreover, when its attribution to Him was known, and then "the abode of peace" came, it is to be understood in light of what is known.

Also, what is customary in the Qur'an is its attribution to its quality or to its people.

As for the first: like "the abode of permanence" (dar al-qarar), "the abode of glory" (dar al-majd), "the garden of refuge" (jannat al-ma'wa), "the gardens of bliss" (jannat al-na'im), "the gardens of paradise" (jannat al-firdaws).

As for the second: like "the abode of the God-fearing" (dar al-muttaqin). The attribution of it to a name of Allah, exalted is He, is not known in the Qur'an. So it is preferable to understand the attribution in light of what is customary in the Qur'an.

Likewise, its attribution to the greeting is weak for two reasons:

The first: greeting with "peace" is shared between the abode of this world and the Hereafter, whereas what is attributed to Paradise is only specific to it, like "the eternal" (al-khuld), "the permanent abode" (al-qarar), and "the everlasting" (al-baqa').

The second: among its qualities other than greeting are those more perfect than it, such as its being lasting and permanent, and the abode of eternity. The greeting therein is incidental, at the time of meeting and visiting, unlike safety from every defect, deficiency and evil, which is among its most perfect intended qualities, constant, without which bliss in it is not complete.

So its attribution to Him is preferable, and this is evident.

When you know these two, the application of "peace" to Allah as one of His names is more preferable than all of this, and more deserving of this name than any other bearer of it, since He, glory be to Him, is free from every defect and deficiency in every respect. He is the true Peace in every sense, while the created being is peace only by attribution.

(Section)

There has been disagreement about naming Paradise "the abode of peace" (dar al-salam). It has been said: "al-Salam" is Allah, and Paradise is His abode.

It has been said: "al-Salam" is safety (al-salamah), and Paradise is the abode of safety from every calamity, defect and deficiency.

It has been said: it was named "the abode of peace" because their greeting therein is "peace" (salam). These meanings are not mutually contradictory.

(Subtle point)

Regarding the attribution of Paradise to "peace," there are three opinions:

The first: it is an attribution to its Owner, al-Salam, glory be to Him.

The second: it is an attribution to the greeting of its people, for their greeting therein is "peace."

The third: it is an attribution to the meaning of peace, i.e., the abode of peace from every calamity, deficiency and evil. The three are interrelated, although the third is the most apparent. For if the attribution were to its Owner, it would have been attributed to a name of His other than "peace," and it would be said "the abode of the Merciful," or "the abode of Allah," or "the abode of the King," and similar.

Moreover, when its attribution to Him was known, and then "the abode of peace" came, it is to be understood in light of what is known.

Also, what is customary in the Qur'an is its attribution to its quality or to its people.

As for the first: like "the abode of permanence" (dar al-qarar), "the abode of glory" (dar al-majd), "the garden of refuge" (jannat al-ma'wa), "the gardens of bliss" (jannat al-na'im), "the gardens of paradise" (jannat al-firdaws).

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 10, verse 31:

If it is said: Does a difference appear between His saying, exalted is He, in Surat Yunus: {Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, or who controls hearing and sight?}

and His saying in Surat Saba': ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah﴾?

It is said: This is among the most subtle, obscure and delicate of these places in terms of distinction. Ponder the context and you will find it to be the opposite of what occurred. The verses in Yunus were brought in the manner of argument against them with what they acknowledged and could not deny: that the Lord, exalted is He, is their provider, the controller of their hearing and sight, the manager of their affairs and other things, and the one who brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living. Since they affirmed all of this, it was fitting to argue against them with it: the doer of this is Allah, there is no god but Him, so how do they worship alongside Him something else, and make for Him partners who possess none of this and are unable to do any of it? For this reason, after mentioning these things of His affairs, He said: ﴿So they will say, "Allah."﴾ That is, they will certainly affirm this and will not deny it. So the thing mentioned must be something they affirm. The addressees against whom this verse argues were only affirming that provision descends from this heaven which they see with their senses; they did not affirm or know that provision descends from heaven to heaven until it reaches them, and their knowledge did not extend to this. Therefore the word "heaven" is used in the singular here, since they cannot deny that provision comes from it, especially since the provision here, if it is rain, comes from the heaven which is the clouds, and it is called "heaven" because of its height. He, glorified is He, has informed that He spreads the clouds in the heaven, by His saying: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, then He spreads them in the sky however He wills﴾. The clouds are spread in the direction of height, not within the sphere itself, and this is known by the senses, so nothing else should be turned to.

Since this is organized around the argument against them, the singular "heaven" alone was appropriate, because they do not affirm the great provisions for hearts and spirits that descend from above that, and revelation is necessary, by which true eternal life comes, and it is more worthy of the name "provision" than rain, by which fleeting, transient life comes. What descends from above that, of revelation, mercy, subtle kindnesses, divine sources, and divine descents, and that by which the upper and lower world are sustained, is among the greatest kinds of provision. But these people did not affirm it, so they were addressed with what is closest to them, such that they could not deny it.

As for the verse in Surat Saba', the mention of their affirmation of what descends from the heavens is not organized within it. For this reason He commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take up the answer in it, and He did not mention of them that they were the answerers affirming it. So He said: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah﴾, and did not say: "They will say, Allah." Thus, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to answer that it is Allah alone who sends down His provision, in its various kinds and benefits, from the seven heavens. As for the earth, the context did not call for gathering it into the singular with the other, since every person, believer and disbeliever, righteous and wicked, affirms that.

And the Exalted said: ﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been fulfilled against those who disbelieve, that they are the companions of the Fire﴾ [Ghafir 40:6].

So the word that was fulfilled is two words: the word of misguidance and the word of punishment, as the Exalted said: ﴿But the word of punishment has been fulfilled against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Zumar 39:71].

His word, glorified is He, was only fulfilled against them through punishment because of their disbelief. Thus the word of His proof was fulfilled against them, and the word of His justice through His punishment.

The sum of all this is that Allah, glorified is He, commanded the servants to conform to His religious will concerning them, not to their own desires. Those who obey Him preferred Allah and His will over their own will, so they deserved His honour. Those who disobey Him preferred their own will over His will. Allah, glorified is He, knew that they would never prefer His will, but would only prefer their desires and their wills. So He commanded them and forbade them. Through His command and prohibition there became manifest, from the decree (qadar) that He had decreed for them, their preference of their own desires and wills over the pleasure of their Lord and His will. Thus the proof of His justice was established against them through their disobedience, and He punished them for their wrongdoing.

(Section)

As for the cosmic (kawniyya) words, they are like His saying: ﴿Thus has the word of your Lord been fulfilled against those who transgressed, that they will not believe﴾ [Yunus 10:33].

And His saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men, all together"﴾ [Hud 11:119].

And the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah, which no righteous nor wicked person can exceed, from the evil of what He has created."

These are His cosmic words, by which He creates and brings things into being. If the religious words were the ones by which He commands and forbids, then the wicked and the disbelievers would not be able to exceed them, since they are the ones they transgress.

As for the religious (dini) words, they are like His saying: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah﴾ [al-Tawba 9:6], where what is meant is the Qur'an.

And the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning women: "You have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah," meaning by His permission and His religion. And His saying: ﴿So marry what is lawful to you of women﴾ [al-Nisa 4:3].

Both types are combined in His saying: ﴿And she affirmed the words of her Lord and His scriptures﴾ [al-Tahrim 66:12]. So His scriptures are His words by which He commands, forbids, makes lawful and makes unlawful, and His words by which He creates and brings things into being. Thus He informed that they are not the words of the Jahmiyya (a theological sect) who deny the words of His religion and the words of His creation, and make them a created thing among His creations.

(Fa'idah)

Ibn Qutaybah and Ibn al-Anbari disagreed about which of hearing (al-sam') and sight (al-basar) is superior. Ibn Qutaybah preferred hearing, and a group agreed with him. He argued with the words of the Exalted: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you. Can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not reason? And among them are those who look at you. Can you guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾

He said: "Since the Almighty paired the loss of hearing with the loss of reason, but paired the loss of sight only with the loss of sight, this is evidence that hearing is superior." Ibn al-Anbari said: "This is a mistake. How can hearing be superior, when through sight comes facing and turning away, nearness to salvation and distance from destruction, and by it the beauty of the face is attained, while its loss is a disfigurement? In a hadith: 'Whoever loses his two precious things (kareematayh) and is patient and seeks reward, I will not accept for him any reward short of Paradise.'"

He answered what Ibn Qutaybah had mentioned: that what God negated together with hearing is equivalent to what He negated of sight, as if He intended the sight of the hearts and not the sight of the eyes. What the heart sees is what it understands, because these verses were revealed concerning a people of the Jews who would listen to the speech of the Prophet (ﷺ), confirm its truth, and then deny it. So God revealed about them: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear?﴾, meaning those who turn away, even though they do not reason; and ﴿among them are those who look at you﴾ with a defective eye: ﴿Can you guide the blind?﴾, meaning those who turn away, even though they do not see.

He said: "There is no proof in giving hearing precedence over sight here, for He has informed us in His saying: ﴿The likeness of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing﴾."

I say: Those who favour hearing argue that through it the highest happiness is attained, by hearing the words of God and the speech of His Messenger. They said: through it beneficial knowledge is acquired. They said: through it one perceives the present and the absent, the sensible and the intelligible, so there is no comparison between what sight perceives and what hearing perceives.

They said: for this reason, the one who lacks hearing is less knowledgeable than the one who lacks sight; indeed, a blind person may be one of the great scholars, whereas no scholar of this kind has ever been known to lack the faculty of hearing.

Those who favour sight said: the greatest of blessings in the Hereafter is looking upon the Lord, the Exalted, and this happens through sight. What sight perceives does not admit error, unlike what is heard, in which error, falsehood and illusion occur. So the perception of sight is more complete and perfect.

They said: moreover, its locus is more excellent, more perfect and greater in wonder than the locus of hearing, due to its nobility and merit.

Our shaykh said: "The truth is that hearing has a distinction and sight has a distinction. The distinction of hearing is generality and comprehensiveness, and the distinction of sight is perfection and completeness of perception. Hearing is more general and more comprehensive, and sight is more complete and perfect. So the former is superior in respect of the comprehensiveness of its perception, and the latter is superior in respect of the perfection of its perception."

(Fa'idah)

Ibn Qutaybah and Ibn al-Anbari disagreed about which of hearing (al-sam') and sight (al-basar) is superior. Ibn Qutaybah preferred hearing, and a group agreed with him. He argued with the words of the Exalted: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you. Can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not reason? And among them are those who look at you. Can you guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾

He said: "Since the Almighty paired the loss of hearing with the loss of reason, but paired the loss of sight only with the loss of sight, this is evidence that hearing is superior." Ibn al-Anbari said: "This is a mistake. How can hearing be superior, when through sight comes facing and turning away, nearness to salvation and distance from destruction, and by it the beauty of the face is attained, while its loss is a disfigurement? In a hadith: 'Whoever loses his two precious things (kareematayh) and is patient and seeks reward, I will not accept for him any reward short of Paradise.'"

He answered what Ibn Qutaybah had mentioned: that what God negated together with hearing is equivalent to what He negated of sight, as if He intended the sight of the hearts and not the sight of the eyes. What the heart sees is what it understands, because these verses were revealed concerning a people of the Jews who would listen to the speech of the Prophet (ﷺ), confirm its truth, and then deny it. So God revealed about them: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear?﴾, meaning those who turn away, even though they do not reason; and ﴿among them are those who look at you﴾ with a defective eye: ﴿Can you guide the blind?﴾, meaning those who turn away, even though they do not see.

He said: "There is no proof in giving hearing precedence over sight here, for He has informed us in His saying: ﴿The likeness of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing﴾."

I say: Those who favour hearing argue that through it the highest happiness is attained, by hearing the words of God and the speech of His Messenger. They said: through it beneficial knowledge is acquired. They said: through it one perceives the present and the absent, the sensible and the intelligible, so there is no comparison between what sight perceives and what hearing perceives.

They said: for this reason, the one who lacks hearing is less knowledgeable than the one who lacks sight; indeed, a blind person may be one of the great scholars, whereas no scholar of this kind has ever been known to lack the faculty of hearing.

Those who favour sight said: the greatest of blessings in the Hereafter is looking upon the Lord, the Exalted, and this happens through sight. What sight perceives does not admit error, unlike what is heard, in which error, falsehood and illusion occur. So the perception of sight is more complete and perfect.

They said: moreover, its locus is more excellent, more perfect and greater in wonder than the locus of hearing, due to its nobility and merit.

Our shaykh said: "The truth is that hearing has a distinction and sight has a distinction. The distinction of hearing is generality and comprehensiveness, and the distinction of sight is perfection and completeness of perception. Hearing is more general and more comprehensive, and sight is more complete and perfect. So the former is superior in respect of the comprehensiveness of its perception, and the latter is superior in respect of the perfection of its perception."

[Section: On the mufti swearing to confirm a ruling]

It is permissible for the mufti (jurisconsult) and the debater to swear to the establishment of a ruling in his own view, even if his oath does not necessitate its establishment for the questioner and the opponent. This is so that the questioner and the opponent perceive that he is certain and assured of what he has said to them, and that he is not doubtful about it. Two men debated an issue, and one of them swore to what he believed. His opponent said to him: "The ruling is not established by your oath." He replied: "I did not swear so that the ruling would be established for you, but to make you aware that I am upon certainty and insight regarding my statement, and that your doubt does not alter, in the face of my certainty, what I am resolute about."

Indeed, Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to swear to the establishment of the truth that he brought, in three places of His Book. The first is: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed the truth."﴾ [Yunus: 53]

The second is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you, the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [Saba': 3]

The third is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected."﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7]

The Prophet ﷺ also swore to what he reported of the truth in more than eighty places, and these are found in the Sahihs and the Musnads. The Companions — may Allah be pleased with them — would swear regarding fatwas and narration. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah ennoble his face, said to Ibn ʿAbbas regarding temporary marriage (mut'ah): "You are a bewildered man. Look at what you issue as a fatwa regarding temporary marriage. By Allah, and I bear witness by Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did forbid it."

When ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — assumed office, he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "O people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted temporary marriage three times, then forbade it three times. So I swear by Allah an oath that I will not find anyone from among the Muslims practising temporary marriage except that I will stone him, unless he brings four Muslims who testify that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted it after having forbidden it."

Al-Shafiʿi also swore in some of his answers. Muhammad ibn al-Hakam said: "I asked al-Shafiʿi — may Allah be pleased with him — about temporary marriage: Was there in it divorce, inheritance, maintenance, or testimony?" He said: "No, by Allah, I do not know."

Yazid ibn Harun said: "Whoever says the Qur'an is created, or that some part of it is created, he is, by Allah, a heretic in my view."

He was asked about the hadith of Jarir concerning the vision (of Allah), and he said: "By Allah, besides whom there is no god, whoever denies it, they are nothing but heretics." As for Imam Ahmad — may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him — he swore regarding a number of his fatwas.

It was said to him: "Should a man add to his ablution beyond three times?" He said: "No, by Allah, except a man afflicted, meaning with waswasah (obsessive doubt)."

He was asked about a man running his fingers through his beard when performing ablution, and he said: "Yes, by Allah."

He was asked: "Is a man in jihad, between the two lines, permitted to challenge a non-Arab warrior to single combat without the leader's permission?" He said: "No, by Allah."

He was asked: "Do you dislike prayer in the maqsurah?" He said: "Yes, by Allah." I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: This was when the maqsurah was reserved for the rulers and their retinue.

He was asked: "Is a man rewarded for hating those who oppose the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes, by Allah."

He was asked: "Is whoever says the Qur'an is created a disbeliever?" He said: "Yes, by Allah." He was asked: "Is there any hadith authenticated for you concerning nabidh?" He said: "By Allah, no single hadith has been authenticated for me except one prohibiting it."

Muhammad ibn ʿAwn said to him: "O Abu ʿAbd Allah, they say that you stopped at (the view regarding) ʿUthman." He said: "They lied about me, by Allah. I only narrated to them the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: 'We used to rank the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: Abu Bakr, then ʿUmar, then ʿUthman, then ʿAli. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not disapprove of it, nor did the Prophet ﷺ say: Do not prefer one over another after these.' So whoever stops at ʿUthman and does not place ʿAli in fourth place, peace be upon him, is upon other than the Sunnah."

Ahmad was asked: "Is residing at the frontier (thaghr) better than residing in Makkah?" He said: "Yes, by Allah."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 10, verse 57:

It is a healing for what is in the breasts from the disease of ignorance and error, for ignorance is a disease whose cure is knowledge and guidance, and error is a disease whose cure is right conduct (rushd). Allah, glorified is He, has absolved His Prophet of these two afflictions, so He said:

﴿By the star when it sets, your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred.﴾

And His Messenger ﷺ described his successors by their opposites, so he said: "Hold fast to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided, rightly-directed caliphs after me."

He made His speech an admonition for people in general, guidance and mercy for those who believe in it in particular, and a complete healing for what is in the breasts. Whoever seeks healing through it is healed and cured of his illness, and whoever does not seek healing through it, then he is as it was said:

"When he is cured of one disease, he thinks he has been saved, while the disease that will kill him remains within him."

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾ [al-Isra: 82]

The more apparent view is that "min" here is for specifying the kind, so the entire Qur'an is a healing and a mercy for the believers.

(Benefit)

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers.﴾

He made the admonition and the healing general, and specified guidance and knowledge. It is itself a healing, whether one seeks healing through it or not. Allah has not described anything in His Book as healing except the Qur'an and honey; these are the two healings. This is the healing of hearts from the diseases of their error and misguidance and the ailments of their doubts and desires. And that is healing for bodies from many of their illnesses, humors and afflictions. Indeed, during my stay in Makkah, various illnesses afflicted me, and there was no physician there nor medicines as in other cities, so I sought healing with honey and Zamzam water, and I saw in them a wondrous healing. Reflect on His, glorified and exalted is He, informing about the Qur'an that it is itself a healing, and He said about honey: ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾. What is itself a healing is more eloquent than what has been made to contain healing. This is not the place to exhaust the benefits and uses of honey.

[Section: On the Qur'an containing the remedies of the heart and its cure from all its diseases]

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts﴾ [Yunus: 57]

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra: 82].

It has already been mentioned that the sum of the heart's diseases are the diseases of doubts (shubuhat) and desires (shahawat).

The Qur'an is a healing for both types. In it are clear proofs and decisive demonstrations that distinguish truth from falsehood, so the diseases of doubt that corrupt knowledge, conception and perception disappear, such that one sees things as they really are. Under the vault of heaven there is no book containing proofs and signs for lofty matters—such as monotheism (tawhid), affirmation of the divine attributes, affirmation of the Resurrection and prophethood, and refutation of false sects and corrupt opinions—like the Qur'an. It is sufficient for all of that, containing it in the most complete and finest manner, closest to the intellects, and most eloquent in exposition. It is truly the healing from the afflictions of doubt and suspicion, but that depends on understanding it and knowing its intended meaning. Whoever Allah grants this sees truth and falsehood directly with his heart, as one sees night and day, and he knows that whatever else is in people's books, opinions and rationalizations is a mixture of sciences in which there is no trust, but are merely opinions and imitation; a mixture of false conjectures that avail nothing against the truth; a mixture of correct matters in which there is no benefit for the heart; and a mixture of correct sciences whose path to attaining them they have made difficult and whose proofs they have prolonged, despite their little benefit. They are like:

"The meat of a lean camel on the top of a rugged mountain: neither easy to ascend, nor fat enough to be worth the climb."

Whatever is best in the possession of the theologians (mutakallimun) and others is found in the Qur'an with more sound affirmation and finer explanation. They have nothing but affectation, prolixity and complication, as it was said:

"Were it not for rivalry in worldly life, the books of debate would not have been composed, neither al-Mughni nor al-'Umad."

"They untie knots by their own claim, but by what they composed the knots only increased."

They claim that by what they have composed they repel doubts and suspicions, but the intelligent, discerning person knows that doubts and suspicions have increased through it.

It is impossible that healing, guidance, knowledge and certainty would not be attained from the Book of Allah and the words of His Messenger, while they are attained from the speech of these bewildered, doubting, skeptical people, whose final course of thought, as one who looked at the end of their advances reports, is what he reached in their inheritance, when he says:

"The end of the advance of intellects is a fetter, and most of the striving of the worlds is misguidance."

"Our spirits are in estrangement from our bodies, and the outcome of our world is harm and ruin."

"Nor have we gained from our research over our lifetime anything except that we gathered in it 'it was said' and 'they said'."

I have contemplated the methods of kalam and the approaches of philosophy, and I have not found them to heal the sick or quench the thirst. I found the closest path to be the path of the Qur'an. I read in affirmation: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], ﴿To Him ascend good words, and righteous deeds raise them﴾ [Fatir: 10], and I read in negation: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11], ﴿and they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 110].

Whoever has tested as I tested knows as I know.

This is his poetry and wording at the end of his books, and he was the most excellent of the people of his time absolutely in the science of kalam and philosophy. The statements of his peers on this matter are very numerous; we have mentioned them in the book al-Sawa'iq and elsewhere.

We have also mentioned the saying of some of the knowers regarding these people's speech: "The final end of the theologians is doubt, and the final end of the Sufis is ecstatic utterance (shath)."

The Qur'an brings you to the very certainty in these matters, which are the highest matters of the servants; for this reason the One who spoke it sent it down, made it a healing for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.

As for its healing of the disease of desires, that is through the wisdom and fine admonition it contains, by encouragement and warning, asceticism regarding this world, desire for the Hereafter, parables and stories containing various kinds of lessons and insight. The sound heart, when it perceives this, desires what benefits it in its livelihood and its return, and turns away from what harms it, so the heart becomes loving of right conduct and hating of error.

Thus the Qur'an removes the diseases that direct corrupt wills, so the heart is set right, its will is set right, and it returns to the nature upon which it was created, and its voluntary, acquired actions are set right, just as the body, by its health and soundness, returns to its natural state, so that it accepts nothing but the truth, just as the infant accepts nothing but milk.

"The youth returned like a child, accepting nothing except pure milk, and his blamers rested."

Thus the heart is nourished by faith and the Qur'an with what purifies, strengthens, supports, gladdens, delights and invigorates it, and establishes its sovereignty, just as the body is nourished by what makes it grow and strong.

Both the heart and the body need to be raised, so that they grow and increase until they are complete and sound. Just as the body needs to thrive through wholesome nourishment and abstention from what harms it, not growing except by giving it what benefits and withholding what harms, so the heart does not thrive, grow, or attain its full soundness except by this, and it has no route to attaining that except from the Qur'an. If it reaches anything of it from elsewhere, that is a meager little, which does not attain the complete goal. Likewise the crop is not complete except by these two matters; then it is said: the crop thrived and became complete.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 10, verse 58 (part 1 of 3):

The statements of the early generations (al-salaf) have revolved around the view that the grace of Allah (fadl Allah) and His mercy (rahmatuhu) are Islam and the Sunnah (sunna). According to the life of the heart is its joy in these two. The more firmly rooted it is in them, the greater its joy becomes, to the point that the heart dances with joy when it touches the spirit of the Sunnah, while people are at their most sorrowful, and it is filled with security when people are at their most fearful.

The Sunnah is the strong fortress of Allah, whoever enters it is among those who are secure, and its greatest gate, whoever enters it is among those who arrive (at Allah). Its people are carried by it even when their deeds have left them behind, and its light runs before them when the lights of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'a) and hypocrisy (al-nifaq) are extinguished. The people of the Sunnah (ahl al-sunna) are those whose faces are made bright when the faces of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'a) are blackened. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106], the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: "The faces of the people of the Sunnah and unity (al-i'tilaf) will turn white, and the faces of the people of innovation and division (al-tafarruq) will turn black."

It is life and light, by which the servant's happiness, guidance and success are (achieved). Allah, Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose example is in darkness, from which he will never emerge?...﴾ [al-An'am: 122].

So the companion of the Sunnah has a living heart, an illuminated heart, and the companion of innovation has a dead heart, a darkened one.

Allah, glory be to Him, has mentioned these two principles in His Book in more than one place, and made them the attribute of the people of faith, and made their opposite the attribute of whoever has departed from faith. The living, illuminated heart is the one that understands from Allah, submits, comprehends from Him, and yields to His Oneness and to following what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent with. "And the dead, dark heart is the one that does not understand from Allah, nor yields to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent with." For this reason He, glory be to Him, describes this type of people as dead, not alive, and as being in darkness from which they do not emerge. Therefore darkness dominates them in all their directions: their hearts are dark, seeing truth in the form of falsehood and falsehood in the form of truth; their deeds are dark, their words are dark, all their states are dark, and their graves are filled with darkness upon them.

When the lights are divided at the bridge (al-jisr) for crossing over it, they remain in darkness, and their entry into the Fire is dark. This darkness is the one in which creation was first created. Whoever Allah, glory be to Him and Exalted, wills happiness for, He brings him out of it into the light, and whoever He wills misery for, He leaves him in it, as Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: («Indeed Allah created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light. Whoever is struck by that light is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray. Therefore I say: the pen has dried over the knowledge of Allah»). The Prophet ﷺ used to ask Allah, the Exalted, to place light in his heart, his hearing, his sight, his hair, his skin, his flesh, his bones, his blood, above him, below him, to his right, to his left, before him and behind him, and to make his very self light. Thus he ﷺ asked for light for his essence, for his parts, for his outward and inward senses, and for his six directions.

And Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The believer's entrance is from light, his exit is from light, his speech is light, and his deed is light..." This light, according to its strength and weakness, will appear to its owner on the Day of Resurrection, and it will run before him and on his right. Among people there is one whose light is like the sun, another like the star, another like the tall palm tree, and another less than that, until among them is one given a light on the tip of his big toe that shines once and goes out another time, just as the light of his faith and following was in this world, so it is exactly this that appears there to the senses and to sight.

(Section)
The expressions of the early generations have varied in explaining grace (fadl) and mercy (rahma), and the correct view is that they are guidance and blessing: His grace is His guidance, and His mercy is His blessing. For this reason He joins guidance and blessing, as in His saying in Surat al-Fatiha: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor﴾. Among this is His saying to His Prophet, reminding him of His blessings upon him: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge? And find you lost and guide you? And find you poor and make you self-sufficient?﴾ So He combined His guidance to him with His blessing upon him through giving him refuge and enriching him. Among this is the saying of Noah: ﴿O my people, do you see, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself...﴾ and the saying of Shu'ayb: ﴿Do you see, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has provided me from Himself with good provision?﴾ And He said about al-Khidr: ﴿So they found a servant of Our servants whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us﴾. And He said to His Messenger: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows, and complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path, and that Allah may aid you with mighty aid﴾. And He said: ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know, and the grace of Allah upon you has been great﴾. And He said: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure﴾. So His grace is His guidance, His mercy, His blessing, His kindness toward them and His goodness to them. And He said: ﴿Then if guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will not go astray nor suffer﴾. Guidance is that which protects from error, and mercy is that which protects from misery. This is what He mentioned at the beginning of the surah in His saying Ta-Ha: ﴿We did not send down to you the Qur'an that you should be distressed﴾, combining for him the sending down of the Qur'an upon him and the negation of misery from him, just as He said at its end concerning his followers: ﴿will not go astray nor suffer﴾. So guidance, grace, blessing and mercy are inseparable from one another, just as error and misery are inseparable, neither of them separated from the other. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed the criminals are in error and burning﴾.

"Sa'ar" (suffering, blaze) is the plural of "sa'ir" (blaze), which is the punishment that is the ultimate of misery. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind; they have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless﴾. And He, the Exalted, said about them: ﴿And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾. Among this is that He, glory be to Him, combines guidance with expansion of the breast and a good life, and error with constriction of the breast and a constricted livelihood. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whoever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted﴾. And He said: ﴿So is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam and who is upon light from his Lord...?﴾ Likewise He combines guidance with turning in repentance (inaba), and error with hardness of heart. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah chooses whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah; those are in manifest error﴾.

(Benefit)
Guidance, mercy and what follows them of grace and blessing are all from the attribute of giving, while misguidance, punishment and what follows them are from the attribute of withholding. He, glory be to Him, turns His creation between His giving and His withholding, and all of that proceeds from perfect wisdom, complete sovereignty and complete praise. There is no god but Allah.

(Section)
The purpose of acts of worship and commands is not, in the primary intent, hardship and burden, although that does occur incidentally and as a consequence in some of them, for reasons that required it and are unavoidable, being among the requirements of this created existence.

His commands, glory be to Him, His right which He obligated upon His servants, and His laws which He legislated for them, are the coolness of the eyes, the delight of the hearts, the bliss and joy of the spirits, and in them is their healing, their happiness and their success, and their perfection in their livelihood and their return. Indeed, there is in reality no joy, no delight, no pleasure and no bliss for them except through that, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers. Say: "In the grace of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ [Yunus: 57-58].

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "The grace of Allah is the Qur'an, and His mercy is that He made you of its people." Hilal ibn Yasaf said: "By Islam, which guided you to it, and by the Qur'an, which taught you it; it is better than what you accumulate: of gold and silver." Likewise Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatada said: "His grace is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an." And a group of the early generations said: "His grace is the Qur'an, and His mercy is Islam."

The verification is that each of them contains both attributes, grace and mercy, and they are the two matters by which Allah favored His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, when He said:
﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was﴾ [al-Shura: 52].
Allah, glory be to Him, only raised up whoever He raised by the Book and faith, and lowered whoever He lowered by their absence.

(Section)
Qatada, Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said, Ibn 'Abbas among them: "His mercy is the Qur'an," making His mercy more specific than His grace. For His particular grace is upon the people of Islam, and His mercy is by teaching His Book to some of them rather than others. So He made them Muslims by His grace, and sent down to them His Book by His mercy. He said: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord﴾.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "The grace of Allah is the Qur'an, and His mercy is that He made us of its people."

I say: he means by this that there are two matters here: first, grace in itself; second, the readiness of the recipient to accept it, like rain that falls on land with little vegetation, so the purpose is accomplished through the grace and the acceptance of the place for it. And Allah knows best.

Joy in the Qur'an has come in two types: absolute and restricted. The absolute is what came in reprehension, such as His saying: ﴿Do not exult; indeed Allah does not love the exultant﴾ and His saying ﴿Indeed he is exultant and boastful﴾.

The restricted also has two types: restricted to worldly things, which makes its possessor forget the grace and favor of Allah, and this is blameworthy, as in His saying: ﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair﴾.

The second: restricted to the grace of Allah and His mercy, and this also has two types: grace and mercy by way of the cause, and grace and mercy by way of the effect.

The first is like His saying: ﴿Say: "In the grace of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾

The second is like His saying: ﴿rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His grace﴾. So joy in Allah and His Messenger, in faith, in the Sunnah, in knowledge and in the Qur'an is among the signs of the knowers (al-'arifin). Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when a surah is sent down, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had this increase in faith?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾.

And He said: ﴿And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice in what has been sent down to you﴾. So joy in knowledge, faith and the Sunnah is a proof of honoring it in its possessor's heart, loving it, and preferring it over others. For a servant's joy in a thing upon attaining it is in proportion to his love for it and his desire for it. Whoever has no desire for a thing, its attainment does not gladden him, nor does its loss sadden him. Joy follows love and desire. The difference between it and istibshar (glad anticipation) is that joy is in the beloved after attaining it, while istibshar occurs before attaining it, when one is certain of attaining it. For this reason He said: ﴿rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His grace, and they rejoice in those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾.

Joy is an attribute of perfection. For this reason the Lord, Exalted, is described with its highest and most complete kinds, such as His joy at the repentance of the repentant being greater than the joy of one who, having lost his riding beast carrying his food and drink in a barren wilderness, then finds it again.

The point is: joy is of several kinds: the bliss and delight of the heart, its gladness and happiness; joy and delight are its bliss, while grief and sorrow are its punishment. Joy in a thing is above contentment with it, for contentment is the heart's tranquility, its calm and its expansion, while joy is its delight, its gladness and its happiness. So every joyful person is content, but not every content person is joyful. For this reason joy is the opposite of grief, and contentment the opposite of anger; grief pains its possessor, while anger does not pain him, except when accompanied by inability to take revenge. And Allah knows best.

(Great Benefit)
The servant remains cut off from Allah until his will and love are connected to the Most High (bi-wajh al-A'la). By this connection is meant that love leads to Him and is attached to Him alone, so nothing veils it from Him; and that knowledge is connected to His names, attributes and acts, so the darkness of negation (ta'til) does not extinguish its light, just as the darkness of association (shirk) does not extinguish the light of love; and that His remembrance is connected to Him, glory be to Him, so that between the one who remembers and the One remembered the veil of heedlessness is removed, and his attention during remembrance does not turn to other than the One remembered. Then remembrance is connected to Him, and action is connected to His commands and prohibitions, so he performs obedience not merely because He commanded it and loved it, and abstains from prohibitions because He forbade them and disliked them. This is the meaning of the connection of action to His command and prohibition, and the reality of the removal of the causes that move one to act or abstain from worldly aims and immediate desires. Trust (tawakkul) and love are connected to Him such that the servant becomes one who trusts Him, glory be to Him, is at peace with Him, content with the goodness of His management, and never accuses Him in any state. His poverty and neediness are connected to Him, glory be to Him, rather than to anyone else. His fear, hope, joy, happiness and delight are connected to Him alone, so he does not fear anyone else, nor hope in anyone else, nor rejoice in anyone else with complete joy, nor find ultimate happiness in anyone else, even if he receives some joy and happiness from the created. For complete joy, perfect happiness, delight, bliss, coolness of the eyes and tranquility of the heart are only through Him, glory be to Him. Whatever else helps toward this sought goal, he rejoices in it and is happy about it; but if it veils him from it, then grief and loneliness from it, and the heart's agitation at its attainment, are more deserving of his rejoicing, so there is no joy and no happiness except in Him, or in what leads to Him and helps toward His pleasure. He, glory be to Him, has informed us that He does not love those who rejoice in the world and its adornment, and He commanded rejoicing in His grace and mercy, which are Islam, faith and the Qur'an, as the Companions and the Followers explained. The point is that whoever has these matters connected to Allah, glory be to Him, has arrived; otherwise he is cut off from his Lord, connected to his own portion and self, and confused about his knowledge, will and conduct.

(Section)

The mercy that accompanies guidance, for the believers, is of two kinds: immediate and deferred.

As for the immediate mercy, it is what God gives them in this world: love of goodness and righteousness, tasting the sweetness of faith and finding its delight, and joy and happiness at the fact that God has guided them to what He has led others astray from and to the truth about which others differ. They move about in the light of His guidance, walk among people with it, and see others bewildered in darkness. So they are the most joyful of people in what their Lord has given them of guidance. God says: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾ [Yunus: 58].

So God commands His believing, guided servants to rejoice in His bounty and His mercy.

The expressions of the early generation (al-salaf) have gone around the idea that the bounty and the mercy are knowledge, faith, the Qur'an, and following the Messenger. This is among the greatest of the mercies with which God shows mercy to whomever He wills of His servants. Security, well-being, happiness, the pleasure, delight and bliss of the heart, and its tranquility come with faith and guidance to the path of success and felicity; while fear, sorrow, grief, affliction, pain and anxiety come with misguidance and bewilderment.

An analogy for this is two travelers: one has been guided to the road to his destination, so he walks safely and at peace; the other has lost the way and does not know where to turn. As God says: ﴿Say: Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have led astray in the earth, bewildered, having companions who call him to guidance, saying: "Come to us." Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 71].

The mercy that befalls one who has received guidance is in proportion to his guidance: whenever his share of guidance is more complete, his portion of mercy is more abundant. This is the special mercy for His believing servants, and it is other than the general mercy extended to both the righteous and the wicked.

God has joined for the people of His guidance guidance, mercy, and blessings upon them, saying: ﴿Those—upon them are blessings from their Lord, and mercy; and those are the ones who are guided﴾ [al-Baqarah: 157].

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What an excellent pair of gifts, and what an excellent addition." Through guidance they were freed from error; through mercy they were saved from wretchedness and punishment; and through blessings upon them they attained the station of nearness and honor.
